segments: Greenland has never had a single wild penguin. The reason is stranger than you'd think.
Real penguins live only in the Southern Hemisphere -- evolved there sixty million years ago, too far to cross the equator.
But the word 'penguin' wasn't invented for them.
It first named a different bird -- the great auk, a flightless seabird that lived in the icy waters around Greenland.
Sailors later saw look-alike birds near Antarctica and reused the name. The real penguin is extinct, hunted out by eighteen forty-four.
Greenland's actual penguin has been gone for over a hundred and eighty years. Follow for more true stories.

metadata.title: Random But True: Greenland Had A Penguin. It's Been Extinct Since 1844
metadata.caption:
There are zero penguins in Greenland today. But the very first bird ever called a "penguin" lived right there in the icy North Atlantic -- and it's been extinct for over 180 years.

Every penguin you've ever seen on TV is named after a bird that's now gone.

Follow for more strange-but-true animal history.
